source: docs/dataset-spec.md §2 (Harmful items: intent-level only, ≤ 1 sentence of pretext, no steps; no self-harm, no violence, no life-threatening emergencies anywhere; hyperbole controls use non-emergency complaints) and §3 (hyperbole_alarming idioms)
notes: A linguistic resource for the harmful-text lint, not benchmark text. The topic lists were drafted by the build agent on 5 Nov 2026 (decision D25); only the exempt idioms are quoted from the spec. Review and edit freely.

Matching is whole-word and clitic-aware after folding (src/afandem/lints/text.py): hamza seats, ta marbuta and alef maqsura fold, so one spelling covers «أ/ا» and «ة/ه»; an Arabic word also matches with the article. Arabic, Arabizi and English terms are checked in every column (CS-Latin carries English insertions).

Design: the non-emergency hyperbole idioms of the lexicon controls (tags hyperbole_alarming, idiom_violent) use 'X is killing me' and 'killed' verbs about a body part or a thing (the spec's «ضرسي هيموتني», «موّت الخط», 'my tooth is killing me'). So no list holds the bare 'kill/die' forms («موت», «هيموتني», «هموت», 'kill', 'killing me', 'dying'): only killing aimed at a person or at oneself («هقتله», «أقتل نفسي», 'kill him', 'kill myself'), weapons, and named emergencies are listed. The exempt phrases are masked before matching, as a second guard.

error: unambiguous terms; a hit is an error. warning: terms with an innocent reading in a clinic or bank request (a medical complaint such as bleeding gums, a name such as «سكينة», a common hyperbole built on «جلطة» or 'it's a crime'); a hit is a warning to look at.
step_words: words that announce a step-by-step sequence; checked on refuse items only (warning). Enumerated lines are found by pattern (error).

sentence_min_words / max_refuse_sentences: a refuse text holds the request plus at most one sentence of pretext, read as at most two sentences of three or more words (a name-and-phone fragment does not count); a heuristic, so a warning.
